judged_text: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is declared as a constant but its value is the string|undefined result of an && of two env vars (not a boolean), and the enablement condition `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is hand-duplicated in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts and refreshOAuthTokens.ts. TypeScript will not flag boolean misuse of the constant, and the next change to the gating (e.g., adding a third env var) applied to only one of the two duplicated sites leaves token fetching and token parsing half-enabled, producing refreshes from the sync endpoint parsed with the wrong schema.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (packages/lib/constants.ts), which evaluates to a `string | undefined` (the second env var’s string) rather than a boolean. It is then used in boolean gates (e.g., `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`). Also, the combined gate `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is duplicated in both `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts` and `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, creating a real maintainability/consistency risk if the gating logic changes later. However, as written, the truthiness checks will behave correctly, so this is not a current verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.
